# Testament of Simeon — 2
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

**1:1** A copy of the words of Simeon, the things which he spoke to his sons before he died, in the hundred and twentieth year of his life, in the year when Joseph also died.
**1:2** For Simeon fell sick, and his sons came to visit him; and being strengthened he sat up and kissed them and said to them:
**1:3** Hearken, my children, to Simeon your father, and I will tell you the things which I have in my heart.
**1:4** I was born of Jacob my father, his second son; and my mother Leah named me Simeon, because the LORD had heard her prayer.
**1:5** I became strong exceedingly; I drew not back from any deed, nor was I afraid of anything; for my heart was hard, and my liver unmoved, and my bowels without compassion.
**1:6** Because valour also had been given to me from the Most High, through works of might and fortitude of heart.

**2:1** And I became jealous of Joseph, for our father loved him above all.
**2:2** And I set my mind to slay him, because the prince of error sent forth the spirit of jealousy and blinded my mind, so that I regarded him not as a brother, and spared not even Jacob my father.
**2:3** But his God and the God of our fathers sent his angel and delivered him out of my hands.
**2:4** For when I went to Shechem to fetch ointment for the flocks, and Reuben to Dothan where were our provisions and stores, Judah our brother sold him to the Ishmaelites.
**2:5** And when Reuben heard these things he was grieved, for he wished to restore him to his father.
**2:6** But I had been jealous and had not consented to sell him, but had kept him guarded seven days; for Judah sold him in my absence.
**2:7** And I grieved in my soul over him for many days, for I had done a great sin.
**2:8** And Jacob our father sought for him continually; and Leah our mother and all our brothers mourned and were distressed.
**2:9** But I alone rejoiced not, for the spirit of jealousy had hardened my heart.
**2:10** Then after two years I heard that Joseph had been sold into Egypt, and I mourned bitterly; and I repented with great grief before the LORD.

**3:1** Now therefore, my children, take heed to yourselves concerning all the works of jealousy; for jealousy rules over the whole mind of man, and suffers him not to eat or to drink or to do any good thing.
**3:2** But it ever constrains him to destroy him that he envies; and so long as he that is envied flourishes, he that envies fades away.
**3:3** Two years therefore I afflicted my soul, and the LORD weakened my hands and feet because the spirit of jealousy was in me.
**3:4** And I knew that what had befallen me was from the LORD, and I repented and wept; and I prayed before God with my whole heart that the plague of jealousy might be removed from me.
**3:5** And he showed me that because of Joseph I had done this, and I was healed.

**4:1** Now therefore, my children, love each one his brother, and put away from you the spirit of jealousy; for this spirit makes savage the soul and destroys the body, it causes rage and war in the mind, and stirs up to deeds of blood, and leads the mind astray, and suffers it not to act with equity.
**4:2** For even to Judah our brother the LORD gave understanding and long-suffering; for he was among the most merciful of us, and he would have put away the jealousy against Joseph, but the spirit of jealousy in Simeon prevailed.
**4:3** Beware therefore of jealousy, my children, and love one another with good heart; and tell your children also to honor Judah and Levi, for from them shall the LORD raise up salvation to Israel.

**5:1** For the LORD will raise up from Levi as it were a High Priest, and from Judah as it were a King, God and man; he shall save all the nations and the race of Israel.
**5:2** Therefore do you also, my children, obey Levi and Judah, and be not lifted up against these two tribes; for from them shall arise your salvation.
**5:3** For the LORD shall choose a priest from Levi and a king from Judah, and between them there shall be peace, and they shall serve the LORD together.

**6:1** And Joseph was a good man and had the Spirit of God in him; being compassionate and pitiful, he bore no malice against us, but loved us even as the rest of his brothers.
**6:2** Take heed therefore, my children, of all jealousy and envy; and walk in singleness of heart, that God may give you also grace, and glory, and blessing upon your heads, even as you have seen in Joseph.
**6:3** All his days he reproached us not concerning this thing, but loved us as his own soul, and beyond his own sons glorified us; and gave us riches, and cattle, and fruits.
**6:4** Do you also therefore, my children, love each one his brother, and put away envy from your hearts, loving one another in deed and in word and in the inclination of your souls.

**7:1** And after he had slept, his sons carried him up and buried him in Hebron with his fathers. And the days of Simeon were a hundred and twenty years.

---
*End of Testament of Simeon*
